meanings.note: Used both as a noun (오늘이 무슨 요일이에요? 'What day is today?') and adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is really nice today.
What time are we meeting today?

meanings.note: KBS's long-running weekly live K-pop music chart television program.

examples.trans: Music Bank airs every Friday.

examples.text: 이번 주 뮤직뱅크 일 위는 누구예요?
examples.trans: Who is number one on Music Bank this week?

meanings.note: Top K-pop solo singer in The Producers.

examples.trans: Cindy is getting ready in the waiting room.
Cindy's new song is very popular.

나오다.gloss: to come out; to appear (on TV/a show)

meanings.en: to appear on television or a show
meanings.note: In broadcasting, performers 'come out' (나오다) on a program.
Basic spatial sense of moving from inside to outside.

examples.trans: Who is appearing on the broadcast today?
Please come outside for a moment.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters like 위 (rank), 번 (number), 층 (floor).

examples.trans: Our team took first place.
Let's meet at Exit 1.

meanings.note: Bound noun (Sino-Korean 位) paired with Sino-Korean numerals to express ranking (일 위 'first place', 이 위 'second place').

examples.text: 이번 주 차트 일 위 곡이에요.
examples.trans: It's this week's number-one chart song.
She took third place on the exam.

meanings.note: Used for award/chart contenders (일 위 후보) as well as political or job candidates.

examples.trans: Cindy is a contender for first place today.
She is a strong nominee for this award.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun.
Korean speakers routinely use 우리 ('our') for personal family members (우리 둘째 'my second child') or affectionately for colleagues/artists (우리 신디).

examples.text: 우리 가족은 주말마다 같이 밥을 먹어요.
examples.trans: My family eats together every weekend.
Shall we take a photo together?

meanings.note: Birth-order noun for the second-born child in a family (following 첫째 'firstborn').
Ordinal noun in a sequence.

examples.trans: My second child became a middle schooler this year.
The first is a son and the second is a daughter.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner placed before a noun to refer to someone or something already known or mentioned.

examples.trans: That song is really good.
That person is Cindy.

meanings.note: Primary meaning: a friend or peer.

meanings.en: that person / kid (referring to someone younger)
meanings.note: Older speakers often refer to a younger person or celebrity as 그 친구.

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend today.
That kid really sings well.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'fan', used for admirers of singers, actors, or sports teams.

examples.trans: I'm a longtime fan of Cindy.
Fans are waiting in front of the waiting room.

meanings.en: it seems / it looks like (in -ㄴ가 보다 / -나 보다)
meanings.note: Auxiliary verb expressing inference or conjecture based on observation.

meanings.en: to see; to watch; to look at
meanings.note: Primary main-verb meaning.

examples.trans: It seems to be raining outside.
Looks like she's busy right now.

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of 무엇, used both as an interrogative ('what') and an indefinite pronoun ('anything').

examples.trans: Is there anything you need?
What are you doing right now?

불편하다.gloss: to be uncomfortable; to be inconvenient

meanings.en: to be uncomfortable; to be inconvenient
meanings.note: Describes physical discomfort, awkwardness, or inconvenience.

examples.trans: This chair is a bit uncomfortable.
Please let me know if anything is uncomfortable.

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of the bound noun 것, always preceded by a modifier (불편한 거 'anything uncomfortable').

examples.trans: Would you like something to drink?
This is mine.

없다.gloss: to not exist; to not have

meanings.en: to not exist; there is no
meanings.note: Existential adjective opposite of 있다 ('to exist / have').

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
Do you have any other questions?

meanings.en: to not be; no, not at all
meanings.note: Negative copula/adjective; 아니다 alone (아닙니다 / 아니에요) is the standard way to say 'no' or 'not at all'.

examples.trans: Not at all, it's not uncomfortable at all.
That's not my fault.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

meanings.note: Emphasizes a change of state or that a new moment has arrived (contrasting with 지금 'right this second').

examples.trans: I have to go home now.
The performance is starting very soon now.

meanings.note: Indicates that something will happen in a very short time.

examples.trans: The bus will arrive soon.
I will contact you again soon.

meanings.note: Common broadcasting abbreviation of 생방송 (生放送).

examples.trans: The live broadcast starts in ten minutes.
Please be quiet during the live broadcast.

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of 여기에서 (여기 'here' + locative particle -에서).

examples.trans: Please wait here for just a moment.
May I take a photo here?

meanings.en: for a moment; briefly; a second
meanings.note: Used to soften requests or indicate a very short duration.

examples.trans: Do you have a moment?
Just a second, I'll be right there.

meanings.note: Pairs with the verb 찍다 ('to take/snap') in 사진을 찍다.

examples.trans: Shall we take a photo together?
This photo came out really well!

meanings.note: Standard verb used with 사진 ('photo') or 영상 ('video').

meanings.en: to stamp; to dip; to mark
meanings.note: Core meaning of pressing or stamping onto a surface.

examples.trans: Can we take a photo here?
I took lots of photos on my trip.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response.
With a rising question tone (네?), expresses surprise, disbelief, or asks someone to repeat themselves.

examples.trans: Yes, that's right.
Excuse me? What did you just say?

meanings.note: Used in standard polite farewells: 안녕히 계세요 (to someone staying) and 안녕히 가세요 (to someone leaving).

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow.
Goodbye, get home safely!

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다 ('to be / stay'); used in 안녕히 계세요 ('Goodbye / Stay well').

examples.trans: Is the director at his desk right now?
Goodbye!
